project_specification.project_name: nullius — live LLM providers behind the provider interface
project_specification.addition_summary: Extend the providers workspace member (packages/providers, import name providers) with live model backends, so the research loop's signal agent and policy-development agent can make real model calls. Today the member holds the one seam every model call passes through (Provider.complete(Request) -> Completion), the rules on which model may take which role, and the provenance pins. The only concrete providers are RecordingProvider, a tap with nothing live to wrap, and RecordedProvider, which answers from fixtures only. This addition adds: - a stdlib HTTP layer with a host guard, timeouts, bounded retries and secret scrubbing; - an Anthropic Messages backend; - one OpenAI-compatible chat-completions backend that serves openai, deepseek, google (Gemini's OpenAI-compatible endpoint) and self-hosted vLLM; - a registry that turns a pinned (provider, model, version) triple into the right live provider, using credentials from the environment; - an operator smoke-check command; - a composed component. Batch APIs are out of scope: the live backends answer one request at a time and keep the base class's NotImplementedBatchError.

existing_context.stack: Python 3.12 / uv-workspace / stdlib only in the providers member (dependencies = []) / pytest (ruff conventions)
existing_context.test_baseline: packages/providers/tests: measured 2026-10-04, 899 passed (PYTHONPATH=src:packages/providers/src, -n 4, 69 s). Workspace suite tests/ green on main.
existing_context.conventions:
snake_case private modules (providers._name), frozen dataclasses, stdlib only (urllib.request, json), and typed refusals that open with a greppable code word. Each new error class is defined in the module that raises it and subclasses providers.ProviderError. Tests never reach the network: every HTTP call goes through an injected transport callable. Follow CLAUDE.md's Build & Test section.
Existing pieces (read, do not change): - providers.Request(messages: tuple[Message, ...], model: str, temperature: float = 0.0 (0..2), max_tokens: int = 1024). Message(role in {system, user, assistant}, content: str). - providers.Completion(content, model, usage: Usage, finish_reason in {stop, length}). Usage(input_tokens, output_tokens, cache_read_tokens = 0), all non-negative. Completion.model is the SERVING model. - providers.Provider: complete() validates the request, calls the subclass's _complete(request) and validates the answer. check_model(model) accepts any model by default. A provider that pins a set overrides it to raise UnknownModelError. Provider.completion(...) builds a validated Completion. - providers.ProviderError, ProviderNotConfiguredError, UnknownModelError, CompletionMalformedError. - providers.ModelPin(provider, model, version), stored as "provider/model/version" (e.g. "anthropic/claude-opus-5/20260401"). The provider spellings in use are anthropic, openai, google, deepseek and self-hosted. - providers.FixtureStore(root).record(Exchange(request, completion)) writes feature 194's fixture file. providers.Exchange is the RecordingProvider's record. - @register builders live only in providers/__init__.py, because a submodule's @register fires late.
Vendor wire facts: - Anthropic: POST https://api.anthropic.com/v1/messages with headers x-api-key, anthropic-version: 2023-06-01 and content-type application/json. The body has model, max_tokens, an optional top-level system, messages [{role, content}] and temperature (0..1). The answer has content [{type: "text", text}], model, stop_reason (end_turn, stop_sequence, max_tokens, or others) and usage {input_tokens, output_tokens, cache_creation_input_tokens, cache_read_input_tokens}. A failure answers {type: "error", error: {type, message}}. 429 and 529 are retryable, with a retry-after header. A text block may carry cache_control {type: "ephemeral"}, with at most 4 breakpoints. - OpenAI-compatible: POST {base}/chat/completions with Authorization: Bearer KEY. The body has model, messages, temperature, and the length cap (max_completion_tokens for openai, max_tokens for the others). The answer has choices[0].message.content, choices[0].finish_reason (stop, length, content_filter, tool_calls), model and usage {prompt_tokens, completion_tokens}. The cached-input figure is usage.prompt_tokens_details.cached_tokens (openai, google) or usage.prompt_cache_hit_tokens (deepseek). The bases are https://api.openai.com/v1, https://generativelanguage.googleapis.com/v1beta/openai and https://api.deepseek.com. self-hosted takes its base URL from the environment.

category.name: Live Provider Backends
category.feature: System posts one JSON request to a model vendor through providers._live_http.post_json(url, headers, body, *, allowed_hosts, timeout=120.0, max_attempts=4, transport=None, sleep=time.sleep), and it answers the decoded JSON object. - The default transport is urllib.request. Tests inject a callable (url, headers, body_bytes, timeout) -> (status, response_headers, body_bytes), so no test opens a socket. - A URL whose host is not in allowed_hosts raises ProviderHostRefusedError (code word host_refused) before anything is sent. Only https is accepted, except for a loopback host. - Status 429, 500, 502, 503 and 529, a timeout and a dropped connection are retried up to max_attempts. The wait is the retry-after header in seconds when present, otherwise exponential (1, 2, 4 s) with additive jitter from an injectable random. - A final failure raises ProviderTransportError (code word provider_transport) for timeouts and connections, or ProviderHTTPError (code word provider_http) carrying the status and the vendor's own error message. Any other 4xx raises ProviderHTTPError at once, without a retry. - A body that is not a JSON object raises CompletionMalformedError. - The member stays stdlib only. This feature claims packages/providers/pyproject.toml so that no other feature touches it, and it leaves the file unchanged with dependencies = []. - Secret scrubbing: every header value named in a secret-header set (x-api-key, authorization, x-goog-api-key) is replaced by "***" in every exception message, repr and log line. A test passes a fake key and asserts it is absent from every captured output.

System completes a request through Anthropic's Messages API with providers._anthropic.AnthropicProvider(api_key, *, model, base_url="https://api.anthropic.com", transport=None), a Provider subclass whose _complete posts through feature 1 with allowed_hosts {"api.anthropic.com"}. - System messages are joined into the top-level system field. The rest go in messages in order. - The prefix is cacheable: the system text, and the message just before the final one (when there is one), carry cache_control {type: "ephemeral"}. That is at most 2 breakpoints. - A temperature above 1.0 raises ProviderRequestError (code word unsupported_temperature) before any call. It is never clamped. - check_model refuses any model other than the one the provider was built for, with UnknownModelError. - The answer joins the text blocks into content and copies the response's model field verbatim into Completion.model. stop_reason end_turn or stop_sequence maps to stop, and max_tokens maps to length. Any other stop_reason raises CompletionMalformedError naming it. - Usage: input_tokens = input_tokens + cache_creation_input_tokens + cache_read_input_tokens, so it counts every input token. cache_read_tokens = cache_read_input_tokens. output_tokens = output_tokens. - repr(provider) never shows the key.

System completes a request through an OpenAI-compatible chat-completions endpoint with providers._openai_compat.OpenAICompatProvider(vendor, api_key, *, model, base_url=None, transport=None), a Provider subclass whose _complete posts through feature 1. - vendor is one of openai, deepseek, google and self-hosted, and each has a default base URL and an allowed host (api.openai.com, api.deepseek.com, generativelanguage.googleapis.com). Any other vendor raises ProviderNotConfiguredError. - self-hosted has no default: it requires base_url, and its allowed host is that URL's own host. Its api_key may be empty, in which case no Authorization header is sent. - Messages are sent verbatim with their roles. The length cap is sent as max_completion_tokens for openai and as max_tokens for the other vendors. - check_model refuses any model other than the one the provider was built for, with UnknownModelError. - The answer copies the response's model field verbatim into Completion.model. finish_reason stop maps to stop, and length maps to length. Any other finish_reason, or a null message content, raises CompletionMalformedError naming it. - Usage: input_tokens = prompt_tokens and output_tokens = completion_tokens. cache_read_tokens is prompt_tokens_details.cached_tokens, or prompt_cache_hit_tokens for deepseek, and 0 when the response reports neither. - repr(provider) never shows the key.

System returns a live provider for a pinned model with providers._live.live_provider(pin, env=None, transport=None), and it answers an AnthropicProvider for pin.provider anthropic, or an OpenAICompatProvider for openai, deepseek, google or self-hosted. - Credentials come from env (os.environ by default), one variable per vendor: NULLIUS_ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, NULLIUS_OPENAI_API_KEY, NULLIUS_DEEPSEEK_API_KEY, NULLIUS_GOOGLE_API_KEY, plus NULLIUS_SELF_HOSTED_BASE_URL and an optional NULLIUS_SELF_HOSTED_API_KEY. The NULLIUS_ prefix keeps the research keys apart from claw-forge's own ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, which is never read. - A missing or empty variable raises ProviderNotConfiguredError naming the variable, never its value. - The wire model is pin.model. pin.version is provenance only. - providers._live.require_served(pin, completion) raises ServedModelMismatchError (code word served_model_mismatch) when completion.model is neither pin.model nor pin.model followed by a "-" suffix. It answers the completion unchanged otherwise. This is how a vendor silently serving another model is caught. - LIVE_PROVIDER_ENV_VARS is exported as a mapping from vendor to variable name.

System makes one real model call from `python -m providers.live_check --pin PROVIDER/MODEL/VERSION [--prompt TEXT] [--max-tokens N] [--record DIR]` and prints one JSON line with pin, served_model, finish_reason, input_tokens, output_tokens, cache_read_tokens, latency_ms and the first 200 characters of content. - It builds the provider with feature 4's live_provider, sends one user message (default prompt "Reply with the single word: ok") and applies require_served. - With --record DIR it writes the exchange through providers.FixtureStore(DIR).record(Exchange(request, completion)), so a live answer can become an offline fixture. - Exit codes: 0 on success, 1 on any ProviderError (one stderr line with the error's code word and message), 2 on bad arguments. - main(argv, *, env=None, transport=None, emit=print, clock=None) is injectable. Tests drive it with a fake transport and a fake key, and assert the key is absent from stdout and stderr.

System exports the live backends from the providers package. They are AnthropicProvider, OpenAICompatProvider, live_provider, require_served, LIVE_PROVIDER_ENV_VARS, BudgetedProvider, ProviderHostRefusedError, ProviderTransportError, ProviderHTTPError, ProviderRequestError, ServedModelMismatchError and BudgetExhaustedError, all added to __all__. The package also registers a "live-providers" component with @register in providers/__init__.py, and that component returns a resolver object whose resolve(pin) answers live_provider(pin, os.environ). - Building the component reads no environment variable and makes no call. Only resolve() reads credentials. - create_app().get("live-providers") answers the resolver. The test builds the app with create_app() once. - Every existing export and component of the package is unchanged.

System refuses a model call once a token ceiling is spent, through providers._budget.BudgetedProvider(inner, *, max_input_tokens, max_output_tokens). This is a Provider subclass that wraps any Provider and adds each answered completion's usage to its running totals. - When either running total has reached its ceiling, the next complete() raises BudgetExhaustedError (code word budget_exhausted) naming both totals and both ceilings. It raises before the inner provider is called, so nothing is sent. - A call that crosses the ceiling is still answered and counted. The refusal starts with the call after it. - spent() answers (input_tokens, output_tokens). A ceiling of 0 refuses the first call. - A ceiling that is negative or not an int raises ValueError at construction. - check_model delegates to the inner provider. Batches are refused with the base class's NotImplementedBatchError. - The totals live in memory, one budget per instance. Persisting spend is a later spec.

project_specification.integration_points: New private modules providers._live_http, providers._anthropic, providers._openai_compat, providers._live and providers._budget, and the runnable module providers.live_check, all in packages/providers/src/providers/. Their tests go in packages/providers/tests/. Every new file is committed as an empty stub so its claim resolves. Only feature 6 edits providers/__init__.py. Nothing calls the live backends yet: binding them into the signal agent and the policy-development agent is a later spec.
project_specification.constraints: - No test opens a network connection or reads a real credential. Tests use fake keys and assert the key is absent from every captured output. - An API key never appears in any repository file, fixture, log line, exception message, repr or stdout. - No third-party dependency. pyproject.toml files and uv.lock are not edited. HTTP uses urllib.request. - Do not edit .env.tpl, .env.vst.tpl, .env.example, run.sh, claw-forge.yaml or claw-forge.local.yaml. - The existing modules of the providers member keep their behaviour. Only feature 6 edits providers/__init__.py, and it only adds. - No member outside packages/providers is edited. The router member and the order path never import providers. - Do not edit docs/user-journeys/. - All existing workspace tests (tests/) and packages/providers/tests stay green.

implementation_steps.step: Phase 1: the HTTP layer (feature 1) and the token budget (feature 7), in parallel.
Phase 2: the Anthropic backend (feature 2) and the OpenAI-compatible backend (feature 3), in parallel.
Phase 4: the smoke-check command (feature 5) and the package exports with the composed component (feature 6), in parallel.
